text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty HIGH - multiple nodes entering NotReady in cluster infer-usw2 affecting pods with label pool=inference. Auto-remediation attempted (kubelet restart). Investigating.
sarah: Acked. I'm the primary oncall. Seeing a NotReady surge across 6 nodes in the infer pool. latency dashboards show 300ms -> 1.2s 95th for text-gen routes.
raj: on my way, pulling node statuses now. Can you paste `kubectl get nodes -o wide`?
sarah: paste below:
```
NAME                        STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP
infer-node-23               NotReady   <none>   42d   v1.27.3   10.2.3.23
infer-node-24               Ready      <none>   42d   v1.27.3   10.2.3.24
infer-node-25               NotReady   <none>   42d   v1.27.3   10.2.3.25
infer-node-26               NotReady   <none>   10d   v1.27.3   10.2.3.26
infer-node-27               Ready      <none>   10d   v1.27.3   10.2.3.27
```
sarah: kubelet on the NotReady nodes is logging repeated: `I0803 12:14:22.123456 kubelet.go:xxxx] Node controller eviction: pod kill` and `kernel: cgroup: cgroup eventfd wait failed`
maria: any GPU driver errors in dmesg or nvidia-smi?
sarah: grabbing dmesg and nvidia-smi from infer-node-23, 25.
leo: quick note — traffic is configured to prefer eu-west then usw2. If usw2 degrades we have fallback to eu-west models but that adds ~60-120ms and can increase cost.
sarah: nvidia-smi shows GPU driver lost context on node-23 and several `Xid` errors. dmesg shows `NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.`
raj: that points to transient hardware or driver issue causing kubelet to mark NotReady after kubelet health checks fail. Any recent kernel/driver updates?
sarah: no scheduled kubelet/driver updates in the last 24h. But infra-bot reports a kernel update on infer-node-26 2h ago from imagebuilder pipeline.
infra-bot: imagebuilder: kernel patch rolled to infer-node-26 at 10:07 UTC. No rollout to other infer nodes.
ben: I'm going to run quick checks and start isolating unhealthy nodes. Suggest cordon + drain on nodes with GPU Xid errors to stop serving traffic.
maria: +1 cordon/drain, but drain will evict pods — we should scale up dedicated pool or enable fallback model variant to avoid customer errors.
sarah: action: cordon infer-node-23 and 25. raj to execute drain with --ignore-daemonsets and --delete-local-data. ben to kick off an emergency scale up of 2 warm nodes in the dedicated infer pool.
raj: cordon done on node-23 and 25. Starting drain on node-23 now.
raj: drain output:
```
node/infer-node-23 cordoned
pod inference-app-xyz terminating
Warning: some pods failed to terminate in 30s, forcing eviction
```
sarah: thanks. ben, can you confirm scale-up?
ben: scaled dedicated-infer-pool from 16 -> 18 nodes, new nodes joining. Cloud autoscaling API returned success; new instances initializing.
leo: routing note — temporary fallback to eu-west has started activating for some customers; we see a small bump in cross-region cost.
maria: customer impact summary so far: 6% of real-time generation requests returning 503/502 in the last 6m, primarily for customers pinned to us-west-2. Error budget burn is +3% for tier-1 accounts.
sarah: marking customer-facing: yes. I've opened a short-status on status.redwood.ai (internal draft) and pinged growth for comms if this persists.
raj: logs show container runtimes on the NotReady nodes complaining about `containerd: shim reaped` and `runtime: oom-kill` for helper sidecars. Could be cgroup OOM cascade after driver crash.
leo: can we force kubelet restart on the remaining NotReady node(s) once evicted to see if they recover without full host reboot?
sarah: on node-26 (NotReady), kubelet is in a crashloop; journalctl shows repeated `Failed to start Kubelet: failed to create plugin: failed to configure cgroups` errors. I'll escalate to infra.
ben: infra oncall joining. Taking node-26 under investigation. If kernel update on node-26 is the cause, we may need to rollback image or reboot into previous kernel.
infra-bot: infra-pager: kernel-rollback runbook referenced — steps required: snapshot, reboot to known-good kernel, validate GPU hw status.
raj: for immediate mitigation, we've enabled automatic fallback model variant on the router for routes with high error rates. That drops throughput but avoids 502s for many customers.
maria: monitoring: error rate down to 2.1% after fallback and scale-up; p95 latency stable ~650ms. Still worse than baseline but acceptable for short window.
sarah: handoff: I need to go offline for 15m to grab hardware logs and coordinate with infra. Raj, can you own the thread and the mitigation while I'm away?
raj: taking over. I'll keep updates here and escalate to senior infra if node-26 doesn't come back by +20m.
leo: added note — start a Canary routing to eu-west for non-pinned customers to reduce impact further.
maria: created a post-incident ticket PIN-517777 on internal tracker with customer impact, timeline, and action items (kernel rollback, hardware diagnostics, improve node health detection).
raj: status: node-23 drained successfully and will be taken out of rotation until hardware validated. node-25 drain in progress. node-26 under infra investigation — possible kernel/driver mismatch. New nodes from scale-up ready and receiving traffic.
ben: infra confirms node-26 kernel rollback staged, coordinating with cloud team to snapshot before reverting.
raj: TL;DR: NotReady surge caused by GPU driver/hardware fails + one kernel update on node-26. Mitigations executed: cordon/drain affected nodes, scaled pool by +2 nodes, enabled fallback routing to eu-west, started kernel rollback runbook. Customer impact limited to short higher latency and a small error spike.
sarah: back online. Thanks team. I'll sync with infra on next steps and schedule a follow-up postmortem if hardware or rollout issues are confirmed.
infra-bot: incident-bot: incident PIN-517777 created, severity: high, owner: raj, next update expected by 5177771550.
raj: noted. I'll update by then with hardware rollback result. :thumbsup:
